hostOS is ubuntu of the Debian family, read from every worker's os-release. It is what ubuntuHost is decided by, and the one distribution that decides it is Ubuntu, whose NVMe-oF modules are in a package the base install does not carry
enableDriveFormat is set, so every drive listed here is formatted before a storage node takes it: a drive that carries anything is not usable otherwise. This is the line to remove if any of them should be left alone.
vcpuCount is 16, the cores of the memory node chosen on worker-01, which is the smallest of the fleet: the control plane assumes this uniform across a cluster's nodes
maxSubsystemCount is 30, which is the middle of the range this API accepts and not a reading: how many subsystems a node should serve follows from the workload rather than from the hardware
minHugePagesSize is 16G, the huge pages free on the memory node chosen on worker-01, which is the smallest of the fleet
enableJournalDevice is set: every worker hands over one disk smaller than its others, the smallest being 512G (0000:af:00.0) on worker-01, and the control plane dedicates that disk to the journal manager instead of carving a journal partition out of every disk. This is the line to remove if the disk was meant to carry data
stripe is 1+0 as a single-node cluster (clusterMode Single), which protects nothing: the worker hands over 1 device for data, and a redundant scheme places each chunk of a stripe on its own device, so 1+1 needs two. A cluster's stripe cannot be changed afterward
enableMetadataJournal is on, because none of the 2 devices is known to complete a 4K write whole as a storage node will have it. The data plane journals the lvstore metadata pages, so a torn write cannot leave a half-written one behind.
enableChecksumValidation is left to the reviewer. Turned on, nothing in this run says whether it can check any of the 2 devices.
wrote discovered-discover-filt-01 in Draft: 1 workers with 2 nvme devices, in 1 group(s) across 1 node set(s); 3 refusal(s)
